I promised that to Mosaic members in a group meeting, and I need to honor it. I'm glad to see it aligns with what Grant and others have raised about sequencing and informed voting. Second, regarding Evan's recommendation about facilitation rotation — I think that's a reasonable and important safeguard to build into the charter. If there's a risk that any member feels unable to attend based on who is chairing, that undermines the whole purpose of combining these groups. I'd support including a rotating facilitation model and a participation barrier check as part of the 90-day review. Marisol, I'd also want to make sure that before the opt-in votes Grant described, the charter clearly lays out all of these conditions — the 90-day review, the facilitation approach, the accessibility accommodations Noor raised, and the review criteria — so members are voting with full transparency. I don't think I have additional conditions beyond what's already been discussed, but I want to make sure the charter I promised members is comprehensive enough to address everything raised in this consultation.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you, Talia. I appreciate your commitment to making the charter comprehensive. From the Accessibility standpoint, I want to make sure the specific access needs I raised are explicitly written into the charter rather than left to be determined after launch. That means the charter should commit to: providing recordings of all meetings, ensuring asynchronous participation options for anyone who cannot attend live, and scheduling the combined monthly meeting so it begins no later than 3:00 p.m. These shouldn't be framed as optional accommodations to be worked out later — they should be baseline design principles for the combined structure from day one. I'd also echo Talia's point that these need to be visible in the charter before the opt-in votes, so members who have similar access needs — whether they've raised them or not — can see that the combined structure will work for them before they vote. I don't have additional conditions beyond what I've already shared, but I do want to flag that access needs like these often go unspoken, so the charter's commitment to them matters both practically and as a signal of inclusion.

transcript.text: I want to echo Noor's point and tie it back to the opt-in vote requirement I flagged earlier. The two-thirds threshold is a high bar, and members need to see a charter that addresses all of the conditions raised in this consultation before they vote — the 90-day review, the facilitation rotation Evan recommended, the accessibility commitments Noor outlined, and the governance structure Talia described. If any of these elements are missing or vague when members receive the charter, that could affect whether they feel confident opting in, which in turn affects whether the two-thirds threshold is achievable in each group. So from a People Policy standpoint, I'd recommend that Marisol's approval conditions explicitly require the charter to be finalized with all of these elements incorporated before the separate opt-in votes are held in each ERG. I don't have additional conditions beyond the opt-in vote requirement I've already shared, but I want to make sure the sequencing is clear: charter finalized with all conditions included, then separate two-thirds votes in each group, then launch.
